chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Qays, from one of the henchmen of al-Sawād, who said:

I saw Sīmāʾ only a short while ago in Surr Man Raʾā, and he had broken the door of the house. Then he عليه السلام came out to him, and in his hand was an axe, and he said to him: “What are you doing in my house?” So Sīmāʾ said: “Jaʿfar claimed that your father عليه السلام had passed away and that he had no son. So if it is your house, then I have withdrawn from you.” Then he left the house.

ʿAlī ibn Qays said: A servant from among the servants of the house came out to us, so I asked him about this report. He said to me: “Who told you this?” I said to him: “Some of the henchmen of al-Sawād told me.” So he said to me: “Hardly anything remains hidden from the people.”

key_terms.الدَّارِ: The house at the center of the confrontation and claim of ownership.
key_terms.جَعْفَرًا: The person whose claim about the absence of a son is cited in the report.
key_terms.جَلَاوِزَةِ السَّوَادِ: Henchmen of al-Sawād from whom the report was transmitted.
key_terms.خَادِمٌ: A servant from the household who confirmed the spread of the report.
key_terms.سُرَّ مَنْ رَأَى: The city of Sāmarrāʾ, the location where the event occurred.
key_terms.سِيمَاءَ: The named individual involved in the incident.
key_terms.طَبَرْزِينٌ: An axe held in the hand during the encounter.
key_terms.وَلَدَ: A son or offspring, central to the dispute reported here.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe a public sign of the Imam’s existence after his father’s passing?
ai.summary: This report narrates an incident in which the Imam عليه السلام emerged and asserted his right over the house, confronting a man who had entered on the basis of Jaʿfar’s claim that the deceased father had left no son. The narration serves as a historical account connected to the recognition of the Imam عليه السلام and the circulation of news about his existence among people.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Qays, from one of the black henchman who said,

‘I saw Sayma’a only a while ago in ‘Sur Man Rayy’ and he had broken the door of the house. So heasws came out to him and in hisasws hand was an axe, and heasws said to him: ‘What are you doing in myasws house?’ So Syema’a said, ‘Ja’far claimed that yourasws fatherasws passed away and there was no sonasws for himasws. So, if it was yourasws house, I shall leave from youasws’. And he exited from the house.

Ali Bin Qays said, ‘So a servant from the servants of the house came out to us, and we asked him about this news. So he said to me, ‘Who narrated to you with this?’ So I said to him, ‘One of the black henchmen narrated to me’. So he said to me, ‘It is almost impossible to conceal anything from the people’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Qays from one of the security men jalawiza, plural of jilwaz, from the (al-Sawad) rural area of Iraq who has said the following.

“I saw Sima’(a man) soon after the death of abu Muhammad (a.s) in Surra man ra’a (a city in Iraq) who had just broken the door (of the tenth Imam (a.s.). He (the twelfth Imam) came out to him with an ax in his hand and said, “What are you doing to my house?” Sima said, “Ja‘far thinks that your father has passed away with leaving any son behind. If it is your house, I then get out.” He went out of the house.

Ali ibn al-Qays has said, “A servant of the servants of the house came out to us and I asked about this new. He asked me, “Who has told you a such thing.?” I said, “A security man of rural area has told me.” He then said, “Almost nothing remains hidden from people.”
